title: Influence of virtual reality (VR) technology on the perception of fear during outpatient surgical procedures and interventional procedures under local anaesthesia- A randomised, monocentric, prospective study ("VR experience in anaesthesia 2").
summary:
Distraction is a non-drug strategy used during medical procedures to relieve pain and anxiety. A new supportive service for perioperative regional anaesthesia could be the use of visual-acoustic distraction tools in the form of video glasses (2D) or virtual reality (VR) technologies (3D). Some studies have already shown anxiety-reducing, pain-perception-reducing and sedation-saving effects for the use of 2D or 3D glasses during medical interventions.
The aim of this clinical trial is to investigate the potential effect on anxiety perception of the use of two-dimensional (2D) video and 3D VR glasses. The aim is to evaluate whether there is a stronger effect on anxiety perception due to a more intense cognitive distraction in a computer-generated 3D environment through VR glasses compared to 2D video glasses. Furthermore, effects on pain perception will be investigated. Furthermore, effects of analgesic and sedation use, intraoperative complication rates and process times as well as patient satisfaction and acceptance will be investigated in the perioperative area. A secondary goal is to evaluate the acceptance of 2D and 3D technologies by patients and medical staff.
conditions: Sensation of fear and pain during local anaesthesia and outpatient surgery

interventions.name: Patients with ambulatory, surgical procedures with primarily regional anaesthesiological care or patients with interventional procedures under local anaesthesia without the use of visual-acoustic distraction instruments.

Patients with ambulatory surgical procedures with primary regional anaesthesiological care or patients with interventional procedures under local anaesthesia with the use of visual-acoustic distraction instruments in the form of video goggles (2D)

Patients with ambulatory, surgical procedures with primarily regional anaesthesiological care or patients with interventional procedures under local anaesthesia with the use of visual-acoustic distraction instruments in the form of 3D VR glasses.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o Written informed consent by the study participant 
o Age >18 years
o ASA risk classification I - III
o Elective outpatient surgical intervention using a regional anaesthetic procedure or
o Elective interventional procedure (e.g. central venous line or port insertion) using a local anaesthetic procedure according to the established perioperative care standard of the hospital
Exclusion criteria:
o Refusal to participate in the study
o Age < 18 years
o ASA risk classification IV
o Emergency surgery
o Surgery under general anaesthesia or combined general anaesthesia with regional anaesthesia
o Refusal of a regional anaesthetic procedure
o Taking additional sedatives (benzodiazepines and others) for premedication
o Obstetric surgery (sectio/obstetric peridural anaesthesia)
o Known epilepsy
o Known dependence on drugs or sedative medications
o Known anxiety disorder
o Known claustrophobia
o Known spinning or staggering vertigo
